headline: Barrels now tell you when they'll slip
lede: PICK RUSH's two invisible laws — the rolling barrel's catch window and glass's shatter speed — got paint that mirrors the physics: catch rings, a jaw warning arc, a slam column that turns green under the feather. The never-dry picker chose it at the bottom of a worked-off queue, and the belt has been quiet ever since.

notes.text: Grab-read telegraphs merged: green hoop = jaws bite NOW, red hoop = it slips; a descending claw aimed at off-axis cargo flashes a red arc; carried glass over its bin paints its projected fall, red until feathered safe (hoist-height releases hit 9.0 against a law of 8.0 — every high drop shatters, and now you can see why).

The tell imports barrelUpright straight from the sim (the sim exports it now) and re-runs the sim's DISCRETE fall — the textbook continuous formula cries wolf at the 60–63 px boundary where the Euler world lands at exactly 8.0, which the law accepts. A 13-height sweep pins colour-equals-verdict at every release height.
PLAICRAFT S1 stays a wait-state: store dry, nightly grader healthy, line 3 needs one human clap take from Jon's phone; swept and released so the wait costs no lane hours.
QA polish pass filed for PICK RUSH: rival-crane intent is still unreadable — the next honest gap on a very shiny shelf.
